advances:
Gives an exact rowwise two-rail formula, and hence a selector
inequality, for the full cap
\[
\frac12(P+2\lambda-sC_\tau)\cap\{r_j\leq\lambda_j\}.
\]
The two selectors are independent: one chooses the translated upper
rail and the other chooses the translated lower rail.  Thus the formula
retains both the section width and the transverse drift of
\([L_j(t),R_j(t)]\), rather than reducing \(C_\tau\) to one segment.
For the exact rational calibration that defeats every one-segment
bound, exact section integration recovers both full-hull values and
their two positive excesses over \(U_1,U_2\).  Since the formula uses
only compact convexity, it applies to the closures of
\(P_\varnothing\) and
\(\operatorname{conv}(\overline{Q_1}\cup\overline{Q_2})\) in every
canonical single-double system.
author: mp_r384_two_rail_extrusion
proof:
Translate \(H\) by \(-\lambda\) and dilate it by \(2\).  In the
chosen coordinates this gives
\[
2(H-\lambda)=P-sC_\tau.
\tag{21}
\]
The row cap \(r_j\leq\lambda_j\) becomes the halfplane \(u\leq0\),
where \(u\) is the first coordinate in \(P-sC_\tau\).  Therefore
\[
\left|H\cap\{r_j\leq\lambda_j\}\right|
=\frac14\left|(P-sC_\tau)\cap\{u\leq0\}\right|.
\tag{22}
\]

Fix \(u\in D\).  A point in the \(u\)-section of \(P-sC_\tau\) has
the form
\[
(u,v)=(u+st,y)-s(t,z),
\]
where \(t\in I(u)\),
\[
A(u+st)\leq y\leq B(u+st),\qquad
L(t)\leq z\leq R(t).
\]
For a fixed \(t\), the possible transverse coordinates form the
interval
\[
\left[
A(u+st)-sR(t),\
B(u+st)-sL(t)
\right].
\tag{23}
\]
The whole \(u\)-section is an interval because \(P-sC_\tau\) is
convex.  Its two endpoints are consequently
\[
\underline E(u)=
\min_{t\in I(u)}\bigl(A(u+st)-sR(t)\bigr),
\tag{24}
\]
\[
\overline E(u)=
\max_{t\in I(u)}\bigl(B(u+st)-sL(t)\bigr).
\tag{25}
\]
These extrema are attained because the feasible fiber is compact.
Their difference is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline E(u)-\underline E(u)
&=\max_{t_+,t_-\in I(u)}
\bigl[
B(u+st_+)-sL(t_+)\\
&\hspace{34mm}
-A(u+st_-)+sR(t_-)
\bigr]\\
&=\max_{t_+,t_-\in I(u)}\Phi(u;t_-,t_+).
\end{aligned}
\tag{26}
\]
Taking \(t_-=t_+=t\) in (26) gives
\[
\Phi(u;t,t)
=w_P(u+st)+s w_C(t)\geq0,
\tag{27}
\]
so the maximum in (26) is nonnegative.  Cavalieri integration of the
sections, followed by (22), proves (6).  Pointwise, the maximum in
(26) is at least both \(0\) and
\(\Phi(u;\sigma_-(u),\sigma_+(u))\).  Integration over \(D_0\)
proves (7).  Expanding \(A,B,L,R\) in terms of their widths and
centerlines gives (8).

For the exclusion assertion, accepted fact `6d2e762bf26bbce5`
gives from the crossing and \(k<M+m\)
\[
c_j
=\frac{2(M+m+k)}9-u_j-v_j
<\frac{4(M+m)}9-u_j-v_j=U_j.
\tag{28}
\]
But \(H\subseteq K\) and (7) give \(c_j\geq U_j\) whenever its
right side reaches (9), a contradiction.

It remains to audit the calibration entirely by exact section
integration.  The halfspace description of (13) is
\[
t+z\geq1,\qquad 16t+z\geq1,\qquad
t+16z\geq1,\qquad t+z\leq\frac{2003}{2000}.
\tag{29}
\]
Thus in row \(1\), and also in row \(2\) after swapping coordinates,
its two rails are
\[
L(t)=
\begin{cases}
1-16t,&-1/10000\leq t\leq0,\\
1-t,&0\leq t\leq1,\\
(1-t)/16,&1\leq t\leq626/625,
\end{cases}
\qquad
R(t)=\frac{2003}{2000}-t.
\tag{30}
\]
This is the transverse information absent from a one-segment bound.

For completeness, the finite affine-envelope calculation behind
(24)-(25) is recorded next.  Label the six vertices in (11), in the
displayed cyclic order, by \(p_1,\ldots,p_6\).  Merging the cyclic
edge lists of \(P\) and \(-sC_\tau\) gives the following cyclic
vertices of \(P-sC_\tau\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 &\text{representation}&\text{coordinate}\\ \hline
1&p_6-sY_2&(1001/10000000,-32063/312500)\\
2&p_1-sY_2&(9101001/10000000,-313313/312500)\\
3&p_2-sY_2&(9116001/10000000,-313313/312500)\\
4&p_2-se_2&(1823/2000,-1001/1000)\\
5&p_3-se_2&(2077/4000,-2081/4000)\\
6&p_4-se_1&(-241/500,481/1000)\\
7&p_5-se_1&(-1001/1000,901/1000)\\
8&p_5-sY_1&(-313313/312500,9011001/10000000)\\
9&p_6-sY_1&(-313313/312500,9001001/10000000).
\end{array}
\tag{31}
\]
The successive differences in (31) are precisely the merged
successive edge vectors of the two input polygons; the transition
from row \(5\) to row \(6\) combines their parallel edges.  Hence
(31) is an exact Minkowski boundary certificate, not a list of
sampled points.

Clipping the polygon (31) by its first coordinate \(u\leq0\) gives,
in cyclic order,
\[
\begin{split}
E_1=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(0,-205003/2000000),(0,-1/1000),\\
&(-241/500,481/1000),(-1001/1000,901/1000),\\
&(-313313/312500,9011001/10000000),\\
&(-313313/312500,9001001/10000000)\}.
\end{split}
\tag{32}
\]
Here \(E_1=(P-sC_\tau)\cap\{u\leq0\}\) for row \(1\).
The lower and upper section endpoints in (24)-(25) are affine between
the following breakpoints:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
u&\underline E_1(u)&\overline E_1(u)&
\overline E_1(u)-\underline E_1(u)\\ \hline
-313313/312500&
9001001/10000000&9011001/10000000&1/1000\\
-1001/1000&
1796997/2000000&901/1000&5003/2000000\\
-241/500&
758997/2000000&481/1000&203003/2000000\\
0&
-205003/2000000&-1/1000&203003/2000000.
\end{array}
\tag{33}
\]
Integrating each affine width as a trapezoid gives
\[
|E_1|
=\sum_{\nu=0}^{2}
\frac{u_{\nu+1}-u_\nu}{2}(w_\nu+w_{\nu+1})
=\frac{189788263753}{2500000000000},
\tag{34}
\]
where \(u_\nu,w_\nu\) are the first and fourth columns of (33).
Equations (22) and (34) prove (17).

For row \(2\), interchange the two coordinates in (31) and clip the
new first coordinate at zero.  This gives the exact cyclic polygon
\[
\begin{split}
E_2=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(-32063/312500,1001/10000000),\\
&(0,-205003/2000000),(0,-1/1000),\\
&(-2081/4000,2077/4000),(-1001/1000,1823/2000),\\
&(-313313/312500,9116001/10000000),\\
&(-313313/312500,9101001/10000000)\}.
\end{split}
\tag{35}
\]
Its affine section-width table is
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
u&\underline E_2(u)&\overline E_2(u)&
\overline E_2(u)-\underline E_2(u)\\ \hline
-313313/312500&
9101001/10000000&9116001/10000000&3/2000\\
-1001/1000&
408816317/450000000&1823/2000&1358683/450000000\\
-2081/4000&
190075067/450000000&2077/4000&43587433/450000000\\
-32063/312500&
1001/10000000&63501/625000&203003/2000000\\
0&
-205003/2000000&-1/1000&203003/2000000.
\end{array}
\tag{36}
\]
Exact trapezoid integration now gives
\[
|E_2|
=\sum_{\nu=0}^{3}
\frac{u_{\nu+1}-u_\nu}{2}(w_\nu+w_{\nu+1})
=\frac{189623587003}{2500000000000}.
\tag{37}
\]
Together with (22), this proves (18).

Finally, (14)-(16) give
\[
U_1=
\frac{78567343796724046029418470413}
{4243900837176000000000000000000},
\qquad
U_2=
\frac{78567343775504545118989732133}
{4243900837176000000000000000000}.
\tag{38}
\]
Subtracting (38) from (17)-(18) gives exactly (19)-(20), both
strictly positive.  Thus the two-rail identity recovers the full-hull
excess that every one-segment extrusion misses.

An independent Sage \(10.8\) audit over \(\mathbb Q\) formed the two
Minkowski sums, intersected them with \(u\leq0\), and returned the
same vertex lists and rational areas.  The edge merge, clipping, and
trapezoid integrations above are the exact certificate.
statement:
Use the affine coordinates and common area normalization of accepted
fact `6d2e762bf26bbce5`:
\[
r_i=2\lambda_i-s\tau_i,\qquad s>0,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i=\frac{1+s}{2}.
\tag{1}
\]
Fix a row \(j\).  Choose a transverse coordinate so that \((x,y)\),
with \(x=r_j\), is an area coordinate chart in the \(r\)-plane and
\((t,z)\), with \(t=\tau_j\), is the corresponding chart in the
\(\tau\)-plane.  Let \(P,C_\tau\) be nonempty planar compact convex
sets.  Write their nonempty sections as
\[
P_x=[A(x),B(x)]\quad(x\in X),\qquad
(C_\tau)_t=[L(t),R(t)]\quad(t\in T),
\tag{2}
\]
where \(X,T\) are their compact projection intervals.  Put
\[
H=\frac12(P+2\lambda-sC_\tau),
\tag{3}
\]
and, for \(u\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
I(u)=\{t\in T:u+st\in X\},\qquad
D=\{u\leq0:I(u)\neq\varnothing\}.
\tag{4}
\]
For \(u\in D\) and \(t_-,t_+\in I(u)\), define the two-rail
functional
\[
\begin{split}
\Phi(u;t_-,t_+)
={}&B(u+st_+)-A(u+st_-)\\
&+sR(t_-)-sL(t_+).
\end{split}
\tag{5}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\left|H\cap\{r_j\leq\lambda_j\}\right|
=\frac14\int_D
\max_{t_-,t_+\in I(u)}\Phi(u;t_-,t_+)\,du .
}
\tag{6}
\]
In particular, for every measurable \(D_0\subseteq D\) and every
Borel pair \(\sigma_-,\sigma_+\) with
\(\sigma_\pm(u)\in I(u)\),
\[
\boxed{
\left|H\cap\{r_j\leq\lambda_j\}\right|
\geq\frac14\int_{D_0}
\bigl[\Phi(u;\sigma_-(u),\sigma_+(u))\bigr]_+\,du .
}
\tag{7}
\]
If
\[
w_P=B-A,\quad c_P=\frac{A+B}{2},\qquad
w_C=R-L,\quad c_C=\frac{L+R}{2},
\]
then the integrand before taking the positive part is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
\Phi(u;t_-,t_+)
={}&c_P(u+st_+)-c_P(u+st_-)
-s\bigl(c_C(t_+)-c_C(t_-)\bigr)\\
&+\frac12\bigl(
w_P(u+st_+)+w_P(u+st_-)
+s w_C(t_+)+s w_C(t_-)\bigr).
\end{split}
\tag{8}
\]
Thus (7) contains both rail widths and the variation of their
centerlines.

If \(H\subseteq K\), if the row-\(j\) crossing and no-half conditions
of accepted fact `6d2e762bf26bbce5` hold, and if the right side of
(7) is at least
\[
U_j=\frac{4(M+m)}9-u_j-v_j,
\tag{9}
\]
then such a \(K\) cannot exist.

The formula passes the following exact two-rail calibration.  Set
\[
s=\frac{1001}{1000},\qquad
\lambda_1=\lambda_2=\lambda_3=\frac{2001}{6000},
\tag{10}
\]
and let
\[
\begin{split}
P=\operatorname{conv}\{&
(91/100,0),(1823/2000,0),\\
&(2077/4000,1923/4000),(519/1000,481/1000),\\
&(0,901/1000),(0,9/10)\}.
\end{split}
\tag{11}
\]
In \((\tau_1,\tau_2)\)-coordinates, put
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_1&=(626/625,-1/10000),&
Y_2&=(-1/10000,626/625),\\
e_1&=(1,0),&e_2&=(0,1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
and
\[
C_\tau=\operatorname{conv}\{Y_1,Y_2,e_2,e_1\}.
\tag{13}
\]
For
\[
M=
\frac{16038523713803046358461709}
{368394169893750000000000000},
\qquad
m=\frac{60231282059897949}{40000000000000000000},
\tag{14}
\]
\[
u_1=\frac{314859717}{31486000000000000000},
\qquad
u_2=\frac{17306988739}{1153800000000000000000},
\tag{15}
\]
and
\[
q_1=q_2=\frac{3006003}{40000000000000},
\qquad v_1=m-q_2,\quad v_2=m-q_1,
\tag{16}
\]
the exact identity (6) gives, for
\(H=(P+2\lambda-sC_\tau)/2\),
\[
\left|H\cap\{r_1\leq\lambda_1\}\right|
=\frac{189788263753}{10000000000000},
\tag{17}
\]
\[
\left|H\cap\{r_2\leq\lambda_2\}\right|
=\frac{189623587003}{10000000000000}.
\tag{18}
\]
Both exceed their allowances (9), with exact positive differences
\[
\frac{1976913346029573538734329587}
{4243900837176000000000000000000}
\tag{19}
\]
and
\[
\frac{1907026187530232163363067867}
{4243900837176000000000000000000},
\tag{20}
\]
respectively.
